Draw one snake plot per group in a grid of panels

Source: R/facet_snake.R
facet_snake.Rd

facet_snake() splits a data frame by a grouping column and draws one snake plot per group in a grid of panels, so that groups such as participants, classes or conditions can be compared in the same display. Each panel is drawn by FUN, by default activity_snake(), with the group value as its title.

The panels are independent plots: each is scaled to its own data. The grid is set with par(mfrow) and the previous graphical parameters are restored afterwards. It returns, invisibly, a list with the value FUN returned for each panel.

To draw groups of items (columns) rather than groups of rows, use the facet argument of survey_snake().

Usage

facet_snake(data, facet_var, FUN = activity_snake, ncol = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame. It is split by facet_var, and each part, without the grouping column, is passed to FUN as its first argument.

facet_var

Name of the grouping column. Panels follow the order in which its values first appear.

FUN

Plotting function for each panel (default activity_snake()). It must take the data as its first argument and accept a title argument; line_snake(), survey_snake(), survey_sequence() and sequential_dist() qualify.

ncol

Number of panel columns. NULL (default) places all panels in one row.

...

Further arguments passed to FUN.

Value

The panels are drawn on the current device. The function returns, invisibly, an unnamed list with one element per group, in order of first appearance, holding the value FUN returned for that panel (a snake_layout object for activity_snake()).

See also

activity_snake(), survey_snake() and its facet argument.

Examples

# Two participants' prompts, one panel each
two <- subset(ema_beeps, id %in% c("xcVDLRQOwn", "6pig43CFyl"),
              select = c(id, start_time))
facet_snake(two, facet_var = "id", ncol = 1, show_total = FALSE)
